words.name: Words
words.description: using truthful, careful and humanizing language
words.action: Find a respectful way to say something that matters to you.

courage.name: Courage
courage.description: standing by principles and speaking up when something feels wrong
courage.action: Name one small change you can ask for calmly and clearly.

dialogue.name: Dialogue
dialogue.description: listening across differences and making room for understanding
dialogue.action: Ask someone what they would like you to understand, and listen without interrupting.

care.name: Care
care.description: noticing suffering and offering kindness and practical support
care.action: Ask someone how they are doing and offer one manageable way to help.

youth.name: Youth
youth.description: making meaningful room for young people’s voice and leadership
youth.action: Invite a younger person to shape an activity, and follow their idea.

questions.text: After a long, busy week, what would make you feel most at peace?
choices: Spending time with someone who understands me.
Taking a quiet walk in nature.
Having time to reflect and reconnect with myself.
Laughing and being silly with friends.

questions.text: Which message speaks to your heart the most?
choices: Find balance in the world around you.
There is always something to smile about.

questions.text: When you lose your sense of peace, what do you miss the most?
choices: A sense of calm and balance.
Knowing what I truly feel and want.
A sense of lightness and joy.

questions.text: You see people arguing online about an important issue. What would you naturally do first?
choices: Choose words that make the situation clearer without hurting others.
Point out when people apply different standards to different sides.
Try to understand why people see things differently.
Think about the people who may be suffering because of the situation.

questions.text: Your group is making an important decision, but time is running out. What matters most to you?
choices: Making sure the final message is honest and clear.
Staying true to our principles, even when it is difficult.
Making sure different opinions have been heard.
Young people get a real say in the final decision.

questions.text: Which compliment would make you happiest?
choices: You always find the right words.
You’re the same person no matter who you’re with.
You trusted me to lead, even though I was the youngest.
You were there when I needed someone.

questions.text: You have a free day to contribute to a more peaceful world. What would you enjoy doing?
choices: Help young people create and lead their own project.
Volunteer to support people going through a difficult time.
Bring people from different backgrounds together to share stories.
Create a message or story that changes how people think about peace.

questions.text: What troubles you most when people are in conflict?
choices: Nobody is really listening to the other side.
People avoid speaking up about what is wrong.
The people who are hurting are forgotten.
Decisions are made without including those most affected.

questions.text: Someone you respect says something hurtful about another group. What would you do first?
choices: Talk to them honestly, even if it feels uncomfortable.
Ask what experiences led them to think that way.
Check on someone who may have been hurt by the comment.
Suggest words that express the concern without demeaning people.

questions.text: If you had one special power to make the world more peaceful, what would you choose?
choices: Help people who disagree truly understand one another.
Give young people a meaningful voice in decisions that shape their future.
Turn hurtful words into truthful and respectful ones.
Be there for anyone who needs care and support.

questions.text: Imagine a more peaceful world. Which two things matter most to you?
Peace × ____ — What would you love to bring peace into?

values.name: Justice
values.description: Rules and outcomes are fair to everyone.

values.name: Dignity
values.description: No one is humiliated or treated as less than human.

values.name: Hope
values.description: People can believe in a better tomorrow.

values.name: Human Rights
values.description: Everyone has safety, food, education, and a voice.

values.name: Reconciliation
values.description: Broken relationships can begin to heal.

values.name: Solidarity
values.description: No one has to face hardship alone.

values.name: Freedom
values.description: Everyone is free to be themselves.

values.name: Compassion
values.description: People respond to suffering with kindness.

values.name: Dialogue
values.description: People listen even when they disagree.

values.name: Sustainability
values.description: We care for the Earth and future generations.

actions.text: Ask your group whether a small shared task is divided fairly.
Make room for someone who has not had a turn in a shared activity.
Ask what would make one everyday rule feel fairer to everyone involved.
Thank someone for a contribution that is often overlooked.
Rewrite a frustrated message so it describes the problem without belittling anyone.
Use someone’s preferred name and invite others to do the same.
Share one small thing you are looking forward to with a friend.
Invite a younger person to imagine a small improvement and help them try it.
Make a tiny drawing or note about a future you would like to help create.
Ask whether everyone can access the information needed for a shared activity.
Learn about one community resource and share it with someone who asks for help.
Invite someone whose needs are often overlooked to suggest a practical improvement.
Ask someone you disagree with what they wish you understood.
If it feels comfortable, send a gentle invitation to reconnect without demanding a reply.
In a small disagreement, name one thing you both care about.
Offer a specific, manageable bit of help to someone with a busy day.
Check in with someone who has been quiet and let them choose whether to talk.
Thank someone who supports your group behind the scenes.
Invite everyone in a shared activity to choose how they contribute.
Ask a younger person which part of a small project they would like to lead.
Make space for a friend to share a song, story or idea they love.
Ask someone how their day is going and listen without rushing to fix it.
Offer to sit with someone who would welcome company.
Ask what kind of support would be useful before offering advice.
Ask an open question and let the other person finish before responding.
Repeat what you heard and ask whether you understood it correctly.
Invite a friend to share a different perspective on something you both enjoy.
Take a short walk and pick up a few pieces of litter where it is safe to do so.
Choose one reusable item for an activity you enjoy.
Ask your group for one small way to reduce waste at your next gathering.
